title: Coherent derived Hom into a finite-injective-dimension coherent complex
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $K,L\in D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume that every cohomology module of $K$ and of $L$ is finitely generated over $A$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], without requiring $K$ to be bounded in either direction. If $L$ is isomorphic in $D(A)$ to a bounded complex of injective $A$-modules [def-sp-injective-resolutions], then every cohomology module of $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,L)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] is finitely generated over $A$.

source.place: Tag 0G4H, lemma-finite-ext-into-bounded-injective; finite injective dimension expanded by more-algebra.tex Tag 0A5S, definition-injective-dimension.

proof.text: Choose a bounded complex $I$ of injective $A$-modules representing $L$, and integers $a\leq b$ such that $I^q=0$ outside $[a,b]$. Choose any complex $P$ representing $K$. By [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective], $I$ is K-injective. Thus [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], specialized to the one-object ringed site, computes $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(QM,L)$ by $\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(M,I)$ for every complex $M$, where $Q$ is localization. We use the $A$-module-valued total Hom complex of [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex], so all subsequent maps and cohomology isomorphisms are $A$-linear.

source.place: Tag 0G4H, lemma-finite-ext-into-bounded-injective, proof; good truncation written at the complex level as in derived.tex Tag 08J5, remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle.

proof.text: Fix $i\in\mathbf Z$ and put $n=b-i+1$. Let $T=\tau_{\leq n}P$ be the subcomplex with $T^q=P^q$ for $q<n$, $T^n=\ker(d_P^n)$, and zero terms above $n$; put $C=P/T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-cohomology], $H^q(T)\cong H^q(K)$ for $q\leq n$ and $H^q(T)=0$ for $q>n$. Hence all cohomology modules of $T$ are finitely generated. Directly from this quotient, $C^q=0$ for $q<n$. In particular $0\to T\to P\to C\to0$ is short exact in every degree.

source.place: Tag 0G4H, lemma-finite-ext-into-bounded-injective, proof; good truncation written at the complex level as in derived.tex Tag 08J5, remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle.

proof.text: For $r>b-n$, every factor $\operatorname{Hom}_A(C^p,I^{p+r})$ is zero: if $p<n$ then $C^p=0$, while if $p\geq n$ then $p+r>b$ and $I^{p+r}=0$. The formula in [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex] therefore gives $\operatorname{Hom}_A^r(C,I)=0$ for $r>b-n$. Since $b-n=i-1$, its cohomology in degrees $i$ and $i+1$ is zero.

source.place: Tag 0G4H, lemma-finite-ext-into-bounded-injective, proof; good truncation written at the complex level as in derived.tex Tag 08J5, remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle.

proof.text: Apply total Hom into $I$ to the short exact sequence of Step 2. For each $p,r$, restriction $\operatorname{Hom}_A(P^p,I^{p+r})\to\operatorname{Hom}_A(T^p,I^{p+r})$ is surjective by the extension property defining injectivity in [def-sp-injective-resolutions]; its kernel consists exactly of maps factoring through $C^p$. In a fixed degree $r$, only the finitely many indices $a-r\leq p\leq b-r$ can contribute. Taking their product preserves this exactness by choosing one lift per factor. Precomposition commutes with the Hom differential [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex]. Consequently $0\to\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(C,I)\to\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(P,I)\to\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(T,I)\to0$ is a degreewise short exact sequence of complexes of $A$-modules.

source.place: Tag 0G4H, lemma-finite-ext-into-bounded-injective, proof; good truncation written at the complex level as in derived.tex Tag 08J5, remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle.

proof.text: The long exact cohomology sequence [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] applied to Step 4 has the segment $H^i\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(C,I)\to H^i\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(P,I)\to H^i\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(T,I)\to H^{i+1}\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(C,I)$. The two outer modules vanish by Step 3, so the middle map is an isomorphism. By Step 1 this identifies $H^iR\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,L)$ with $H^iR\operatorname{Hom}_A(QT,L)$.

source.place: Tag 0G4H, lemma-finite-ext-into-bounded-injective, proof; good truncation written at the complex level as in derived.tex Tag 08J5, remark-truncation-distinguished-triangle.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-bounded-above-coherent-rhom] to $QT$ and $L$, with upper bound $u=n$ and lower bound $v=a$. Step 2 verifies bounded-above finitely generated cohomology for $QT$. The chosen representative $I$ verifies $H^q(L)=0$ for $q<a$, and finite generation of all $H^q(L)$ is a hypothesis of the item. The cited lemma makes $H^iR\operatorname{Hom}_A(QT,L)$ finitely generated. Step 5 transfers finite generation to $H^iR\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,L)$. Since $i$ was arbitrary, this proves the assertion without a bound on $K$.
